concepts.title: Date Trick Decoding
concepts.definition: A mathematical trick where operations on a month and day produce an encoded numerical output from which the original month and day can be retrieved algebraically.
concepts.formula: code = answer - 165, month = code // 100, day = code % 100
concepts.key_idea: Take away 165 and the month pops out in the hundreds place, the day in the last two digits.
question_patterns: find the date if the final answer is ...
what date corresponds to the answer ...
calculate the starting month and day for answer ...
decode the date from the trick result ...
The trick lands on 1390 -- which date?

solution_steps.explain: subtracting 165 undoes the constant offset in the date trick formula
the quotient when divided by 100 gives the month number
the remainder when divided by 100 gives the day of the month

concepts.title: Three-Row Number Pyramid Top Value
concepts.definition: In a number pyramid where each entry is the sum of two adjacent entries directly below it, the top value of a three-row pyramid is determined by combining the base numbers.
concepts.key_idea: The central base number contributes twice to the apex value, while the end base numbers contribute once.
question_patterns: Frame a topmost task like the chapter exercise and solve it with every step shown.
calculate the apex of a three row pyramid with base ...
what is the top value for bottom row ...
determine the top number of a 3 row pyramid ...
Base 5,1,2 -- what sits on top?

solution_steps.action: compute top value from bottom row entries
solution_steps.explain: apply the formula a + 2b + c using the three base values a, b, and c
the second row holds a + b and b + c, confirming each entry is the sum of the two adjacent entries below it

solution_steps.action: confirm the apex by adding the middle row
solution_steps.explain: adding the two middle-row entries reproduces the apex value, validating the pyramid addition rule

concepts.title: Four-Row Number Pyramid Top Value
concepts.definition: In a four-row number pyramid following the standard addition rule, the apex number is obtained as a weighted sum of the four base entries.
concepts.key_idea: The binomial coefficients 1, 3, 3, 1 determine the contribution of each base number to the top of a 4-row pyramid.
question_patterns: find the topmost row of a 4 row pyramid with base ...
calculate the peak number for a four level pyramid ...
what is the apex value for a four row pyramid given base ...
compute the top number of a 4 row number pyramid ...
Base 1,2,3,4 -- find the apex.

solution_steps.action: calculate the apex from four base numbers
solution_steps.explain: multiply inner base values by 3 and add outer base values
the coefficients 1, 3, 3, 1 come from two layers of pairwise addition, so each base value reaches the apex with weight equal to its row-3 binomial coefficient

solution_steps.action: confirm the apex by summing the third row
solution_steps.explain: the third row entries are a + 3b + 3c + d split across two cells; adding them reproduces the apex value

concepts.title: Calendar 2x2 Grid Analysis
concepts.definition: The sum of four dates forming a 2 by 2 square on a monthly calendar page is equal to four times the top-left date plus sixteen.
concepts.key_idea: Because adjacent calendar cells differ by 1 horizontally and 7 vertically, grid sums simplify to linear equations.
question_patterns: find the 4 numbers in the grid if the sum is ...
determine the top left date when 2x2 grid sum is ...
calculate the dates in a calendar grid with total sum ...
what are the four calendar dates given their sum ...
A 2x2 grid sums to 52 -- which dates?

solution_steps.explain: subtract 16 from grid sum and divide by 4 to get top-left date a
the cell to the right is a + 1, the cell below is a + 7, and the diagonally opposite cell is a + 8
adding all four derived dates should reproduce the original grid sum, confirming the solution

concepts.title: Maximizing Product of 2-Digit by 1-Digit Number
concepts.definition: Let the biggest digit do the multiplying; the other two descend into the two-digit factor.
concepts.key_idea: Given ordered digits p < q < r, the maximum product is formed by placing r as multiplier and q p as multiplicand.
question_patterns: fill the digits ... to make the largest product possible
calculate the maximum product using three digits ...
what is the largest product of a 2 digit and 1 digit number using digits ...
find the greatest product formed by digits ...
Digits 3,7,2 -- build the biggest product.

solution_steps.explain: combine second largest digit q (tens) and smallest digit p (ones)
multiply multiplicand by largest digit r
placing the largest digit in the multiplier position and the next largest in the tens place of the multiplicand yields the maximum possible product for the three given digits

concepts.title: Difference of Reversed Two-Digit Numbers
concepts.definition: A two-digit number minus its flip lands on 9 times the gap between the digits.
concepts.formula: diff = 9 * abs(b - a), quotient = abs(b - a)
concepts.key_idea: That flip-difference never misses a 9 in its times table.
question_patterns: find the difference when a 2 digit number is reversed
calculate the quotient when the difference of reversed digits is divided by 9
what is the result of subtracting reversed 2 digit number from original
determine the quotient after dividing digit reversal difference by 9
Reverse 72 and subtract -- what do you get?

solution_steps.explain: compute absolute difference between tens digit a and units digit b
multiply digit difference by 9
the quotient upon dividing by 9 is simply the digit difference

concepts.title: Sum of Reversed Two-Digit Numbers
concepts.definition: Adding a two-digit number to its digit reversal always results in a multiple of 11 equal to 11 times the sum of its digits.
concepts.key_idea: Summing a 2-digit number and its reverse yields eleven times the sum of individual digits.
question_patterns: find the sum when a 2 digit number is added to its reverse
calculate the result of adding 2 digit number and its reversed form
what is the sum of digits quotient when dividing reverse sum by 11
determine the sum of a number and its digit reversal
Add 43 to its flip.

solution_steps.explain: add tens digit a and units digit b
multiply digit sum by 11

solution_steps.action: verify the result is a multiple of 11
solution_steps.explain: dividing the sum by 11 should return the digit sum, confirming the reversal-addition rule

concepts.title: Cyclic Sum of Three-Digit Numbers
concepts.definition: Forming three 3-digit numbers by cyclically shifting digits a, b, c and adding them yields 111 times the sum of the three digits, which is divisible by 37 and 3.
concepts.key_idea: The sum abc + bca + cab equals 111*(a + b + c) and is always a multiple of 37 and 3.
question_patterns: find the cyclic sum of 3 digit numbers generated by digits
calculate the sum of abc bca and cab
what is the total of all cyclic permutations of a 3 digit number
determine the sum when digits of a 3 digit number are rotated
Add the cyclic shuffles of 123.

solution_steps.action: find sum of the three digits
solution_steps.explain: add digits a, b, and c
multiply digit sum by 111
since 111 = 3 x 37, the cyclic sum is always divisible by both 37 and 3, confirming the algebraic identity
